content.text:
All the queries have run; here are the results.

I could fully answer only one of the six questions. Your account (`emea-analyst`) only sees EMEA rows in the premium and policy data. That means questions 1–3 return EMEA-only figures, not company totals. The catalog has no metric for loss ratio or commission, so questions 5 and 6 can't be answered at all.

**1. Net written premium by region, Q3 2026: EMEA only.** Your access returned one region: **EMEA $343,269.84**. Every other region is filtered out. I've marked this not answered in the JSON because one region would look like the full breakdown. Net written premium is gross written premium minus cancellations, counted in the month the premium takes effect, with quotes excluded.

**2. Gross written premium by product line, H1 2026: EMEA only.** Auto **$134,856.74**, Commercial **$395,649.19**, Home **$154,709.40**. Gross written premium is premium before cancellations, excluding taxes and fees, counted in the month it takes effect.

**3. Policies written, March 2026: EMEA only.** **27** distinct policies (quotes don't count).

**4. Paid on closed claims, Q2 2026, by severity: answered.** High **$18,616.26**, Medium **$17,904.82**, Low **$13,530.45**, a total of $50,051.53. This counts the amount paid on claims that closed in April–June. The claims data isn't one of the limited tables, so this should be company-wide.

**5. Loss ratio by region, Q3 2026: not answerable.** The catalog says outright that it doesn't track loss ratio. Claims paid can't be split by region, so I couldn't build it from other metrics either.

**6. Agent commission, Q3 2026: not answerable.** The catalog has no commission metric, and the commissions table is hidden from your account.

To get company-wide answers to 1–3, you need access to all regions, and the data team grants that. For 5 and 6, the data team would also need to add those metrics to the catalog.
